US Warns of Sanctions Risks for Companies Paying Strait of Hormuz Tolls
American people, companies and banks are prohibited under U.S. sanctions laws from making toll payments to Iran for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, the Office of Foreign Assets Control said in new guidance released April 28.

OFAC said any direct or indirect payments to the Iranian government or its military wing, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, "would not be authorized" for U.S. people, including U.S. financial institutions, or for foreign entities that are owned or controlled by U.S. people or entities.
The agency also warned that non-U.S. people and companies may risk exposure to U.S. sanctions if they make payments to Iran, especially if those transactions involve anyone sanctioned by the U.S. "This includes the Government of Iran and the IRGC, which is sanctioned pursuant to several authorities, including nonproliferation and counterterrorism sanctions authorities, and is designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization."
In addition, non-U.S. companies risk sanctions exposure under other U.S. sanctions authorities, including those that allow the country to designate any person or entity that knowingly carries out certain "significant transactions" with sectors of the Iranian economy "or who have been determined to operate in those sectors, including the financial and petroleum and petrochemical sectors."
Iran has proposed charging a toll for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, which President Donald Trump has opposed (see 2604170073).
